Percent of white in participants.evidence_source: Text states 'Most participants identified as being of Dutch (n = 227), German (n = 37), Belgian (n = 9), mixed-Dutch (n = 7), or Turkish (n = 6) ethnic descent.' Assuming Dutch, German, Belgian, and mixed-Dutch are considered white/European: (227 + 37 + 9 + 7) / 310 = 280 / 310 = 0.9032 = 90.32%. However, Turkish participants (n = 6) are typically not classified as white. If only Dutch, German, Belgian, and mixed-Dutch are counted as white: 280 / 310 = 90.32%. If we conservatively count only Dutch and German as definitively white: (227 + 37) / 310 = 264 / 310 = 85.16%. Given ambiguity in ethnic classification, using the most inclusive European classification: (227 + 37 + 9 + 7) / 310 = 90.32%. Reconsidering: Belgian and mixed-Dutch may include non-white individuals. Most conservative estimate counting only clearly white groups (Dutch + German): 264 / 310 = 85.16%. Using moderate estimate (Dutch + German + Belgian + mixed-Dutch): 280 / 310 = 90.32%. Reported value uses moderate estimate of 90.32%, but this should be noted as an inference.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the participants for a single study (Study X) consisting of 310 Dutch-speaking female undergraduates from the Netherlands with a mean age of 21.31 years and mean BMI of 22.14 kg/m². The majority of participants identified as Dutch (n=227), German (n=37), Belgian (n=9), mixed-Dutch (n=7), or Turkish (n=6) ethnic descent, with the remainder identifying with other ethnic groups. The sample was limited to women due to practical constraints in data collection.
